title: Fixed Shoe Last Anvil and Tripod Stand
description: One newly authored complete static cobbler-style shoe-last anvil stand exterior. Three full low splayed cast legs join independent broad grounded feet to one annular root collar and an entire vertical bored sleeve. One exposed fixed upper stem enters the sleeve and the underside of a full solid asymmetric shoe-bottom-shaped anvil head. The head has a broad rounded forefoot, narrowing middle waist, distinct rear heel and genuine raised underside arch; its lighter upper facets are actual material assignments on the same closed mesh. A separate complete side thumb-screw appearance belongs to the sleeve. All numeric geometry is new, with no old smith anvil, timber stump, boot shell, sole, lace or foot model imported, filled, scaled or reused. Unlike the old rectangular face/conical-horn smith anvil on a bound timber stump, this has a complete shoe-contoured head on an open thin-stem tripod assembly. Unlike footwear it is a closed solid repair-head appearance without a wearable cavity, cuff or upper. One prop, zero scenes, no shoe, person, loose tools or surrounding workbench. Four opaque constant untextured PBR materials, metres, Z up and actual whole horizontal bounds-centred ground origin. Static game-art only: no real shoe size, shaping, repair effectiveness, striking or clamping capacity, adjustable stem travel, screw action, replaceable-head fit, load, stability, manufacture, ergonomics or occupational safety claim.
